title: Batch OutboxProcessor's post-commit deleteRow/markAttempted cleanup instead of awaiting it per row

evidence.quote:
for (final id in ids) {
            await _dao.markAttempted(id, error: failedError.toString());

why: pushCompletionsBatch exists specifically 'to eliminate the N-round-trip problem' by pushing up to _completionDrainCeiling=100000 rows in ≤500-op Firestore batches, but the local cleanup after that push still runs one awaited Drift statement per outbox row. For the large backlogs this ceiling anticipates (bulk_prior_completion_service / bulk_mark_screen can enqueue hundreds of completions at once, or a long offline stretch), this reintroduces the exact per-row round-trip cost DB-3 exists to prevent — now against the local DB — and materially lengthens the drain, which (per the concurrency finding above) increases the odds of tripping the drainStaleAfter race.
recommendation: Add a bulk DAO method (e.g. deleteRows(List<int> ids) / markAttemptedBulk(List<int> ids, {required String error})) backed by a single batch()/DELETE...WHERE id IN(...) statement and call it once per commit/failure group instead of per row.
acceptance_criteria: New bulk DAO method(s) wrapped in a single transaction()/batch(); OutboxProcessor calls it once per outcome group.
Existing K3/K4 BatchPushException accounting tests continue to pass; add a test asserting the bulk DAO method is invoked exactly once for a multi-row commit/failure group.
